out must point to user-owned storage that outlives the timer; do not place on transient stack if timer may outlive the scope.

functions.name: init_single_timeout_until
functions.description: Initializes a timeout_state_t to represent a single absolute-time deadline and returns a checker function (check_timeout_fn) you can call to test whether that deadline has been reached/expired. Typical usage: initialize a local timeout_state_t, call init_single_timeout_until(&ts, target), then periodically invoke the returned function with the same ts to poll for timeout. The returned function has the signature bool (*)(timeout_state_t *ts, bool reset); the exact semantics of the reset parameter are not documented here; based on naming, reset likely controls whether any internal state is reset on that call. Details not present in the header: whether target in the past yields an immediate timeout, whether the returned function pointer can be NULL on error, and the precise meaning of reset.
requirements: ts must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a timeout_state_t that remains valid for the lifetime of using the returned checker.
Call the returned checker with the same ts pointer that was used to initialize it.
target must be an absolute_time_t value (from pico/time.h). If target is in the past, behavior is likely to indicate an immediate timeout, but exact behavior is not specified here.
Do not assume thread safety; if used from multiple threads/cores/IRQs, external synchronization may be required (not specified in the header).
The meaning of the reset argument to the returned checker is unspecified in this header; use with caution or consult full SDK docs.

Typical usage: keep a local timeout_state_t, call init_per_iteration_timeout_us(&ts, timeout_us), then on each iteration call the returned function with ts to check for timeout. The returned function has the signature bool (*)(timeout_state_t *ts, bool reset); the exact semantics of the reset parameter are not documented here; based on naming, reset likely restarts the per-iteration timer when true. Details not present in the header: behavior for per_iteration_timeout_us == 0, whether the function can return NULL on error, and exact meaning of reset.
requirements: ts must be a non-null pointer to writable storage for a timeout_state_t that remains valid for the lifetime of using the returned checker.
Call the returned checker with the same ts pointer that was used to initialize it.
per_iteration_timeout_us should be a positive duration in microseconds; behavior for 0 is not specified in this header.
Do not assume thread safety; if used from multiple threads/cores/IRQs, external synchronization may be required (not specified in the header).
The meaning of the reset argument to the returned checker is unspecified in this header; use with caution or consult full SDK docs.

functions.description: Reverses the bit order of a 32-bit value. Given a 32-bit input, returns a value whose bits are in the opposite order (bit 31 becomes bit 0, etc.). Intended for optimized bit manipulation; use when a bit-reversed representation is required (e.g., bit-reversed indexing or data formatting). Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: Argument 'bits' must be a 32-bit unsigned integer (uint32_t).
Function may be called at any time; no initialization or global state required.
Return value is always defined for any uint32_t input; no error reporting.

functions.description: Reverses the bit order of a 64-bit value. Given a 64-bit input, returns a value whose bits are in the opposite order. Intended for optimized bit manipulation; use when a bit-reversed representation of a 64-bit word is needed. Pure function with no side effects.
requirements: Argument 'bits' must be a 64-bit unsigned integer (uint64_t).
Function may be called at any time; no initialization or global state required.
Return value is always defined for any uint64_t input; no error reporting.
